title: Count Number of Rectangles Containing Each Point
summary: Given a list of rectangles defined by their lengths and heights, and a list of points, determine how many rectangles contain each point.
statement: Given a list of rectangles defined by their lengths and heights, and a list of points, determine how many rectangles contain each point. For a point to be considered contained within a rectangle, its x-coordinate must be between 0 and the rectangle's length, inclusive, and its y-coordinate must be between 0 and the rectangle's height, inclusive.
constraints: Each rectangle [width,height] spans from the origin through those inclusive coordinates.
A rectangle contains [x,y] exactly when width>=x and height>=y.
Return one count per query point in the original point order.
target_time_complexity: O(R log R + P*H log R)
hints: Group rectangle widths by their integer heights and sort each group.
For a point [x,y], only height buckets y and above qualify; binary-search the first width at least x in each.
Sum len(bucket)-bisect_left(bucket,x) for all qualifying heights.
The height loop enforces height>=y and the binary-search suffix enforces width>=x, so every containing rectangle is counted once.
editorial: The height loop enforces height>=y and the binary-search suffix enforces width>=x, so every containing rectangle is counted once.

tests.explanation: Two rectangles contain point [2,1], while only the height-five rectangle contains [1,4].
One rectangle reaches height three, and all three contain [1,1].
